paras: The killing of Carson Hardy was the shooting death in August 1900 of a Black man, believed to be Carson Hardy, whose body was found near Shell Creek, Tennessee, on the E. T. & W. N. C. railroad. Hardy had been arrested on suspicion of burning a barn and, according to the Johnson City Comet, was shot to death while in an officer's charge. The Comet ran the item under the headline "Foul Play Suspected," noting thirty or more bullet holes in the body.

According to the Comet, Hardy had first been arrested for being drunk at Shell Creek and afterward made "some threats against his prosecutors." A few nights later a barn was burned, and Hardy was arrested on suspicion of setting the fire.

While Hardy was in the charge of an officer, he was shot to death; the paper did not say who fired, how many were involved, or where the officer was at the time. The body of "an unknown negro" was found the Tuesday before the paper's August 23 issue, probably August 21, near Shell Creek on the railroad. There were "thirty or more bullet holes in the corpse," and the Comet said the dead man was "supposed to be" Hardy rather than positively identified.
No report of an inquest, an arrest of the killers, or any official inquiry appears in the coverage.

The only report found is a short local item on page 3 of The Comet of Johnson City, Tennessee, published August 23, 1900. Its headline, "Foul Play Suspected," signaled an unlawful killing, but the item did not use the words "lynching" or "mob" and named no one responsible. The paper referred to the victim as "an unknown negro" and set out the drunkenness arrest, the threats and the barn-burning suspicion before reporting the shooting in a single sentence.
No account of the killing was found in other white papers or in the Black press for August and September 1900.

reader.title: Killing of Carson Hardy
bases: A Black prisoner held on suspicion of barn burning was reported shot to death while in an officer's charge and found with thirty or more bullet holes under the headline 'Foul Play Suspected' (A1); the killers are not named, so the type rests on the pattern, not on a reported mob.

A1 reports a man in an officer's custody on suspicion of arson shot to death, his body bearing thirty or more bullet holes, and heads the item 'Foul Play Suspected', which points to an extralegal killing of an accused prisoner by several shooters; but it names no mob, no number of attackers and no motive, so the group and pretext elements are not reported.
Only one report, a short local item in the Johnson City Comet (A1), was found in either press; even the victim's identity is given there as 'supposed'.

accounts.label: Local newspaper item
accounts.gist: An unknown Black man's body with thirty or more bullet holes was found near Shell Creek; it was supposed to be Carson Hardy, arrested on suspicion of barn burning, who was shot to death while in an officer's charge.

framing.detail: Headed 'Foul Play Suspected'; reports the killing flatly, calls the dead man 'an unknown negro', relays the drunkenness, threats and barn-burning suspicion, and names no killers.

record_check.dossier: Date the body was found ('last Tuesday' before 1900-08-23); the shooting date is not reported and may be earlier.
No county is named in the item; Shell Creek and the E. T. & W. N. C. railroad are the only places given.
Identification is tentative: 'an unknown negro' 'supposed to be' Carson Hardy.
Arrested on suspicion of burning a barn, after an arrest for drunkenness and threats against his prosecutors.
In an officer's charge when shot.
Not stated; no mob is mentioned.
